horizon_driver: day-to-day / harvest-to-harvest survival horizon; migration and riot decisions are triggered by acute price shocks, not multi-year planning

constraints.source: transit cost, smuggler fees, family separation, destination-country border enforcement
constraints.breaks_under: local conditions (violence, famine, hyperinflation) make staying costlier than a very high-cost migration, observed repeatedly in fragile-state collapses

constraints.action: organised violent uprising aimed at regime change (as opposed to issue-specific protest)
constraints.source: collective-action and coordination costs facing an atomized, resource-poor population without organisational infrastructure
constraints.breaks_under: protest is captured or organised by an external actor (opposition party, military faction, diaspora-linked social-media network) supplying coordination capacity — Kenya 2024 shows this can shift fast once youth/social-media coordination substitutes for formal organisation

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Governments removing fuel/energy subsidies (Nigeria May 2023, Angola July 2025, Ecuador 2025) framed the moves as fiscally necessary, IMF/creditor-endorsed reforms with promised compensating transfers.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Nigeria's petrol price rose ~300% (185 to 650 naira/litre) overnight in 2023, triggering nationwide protests and a further Feb 2024 wave over living costs; Angola's July 2025 fuel-subsidy cut, starting from a taxi-driver strike in Luanda, produced the deadliest civil unrest since its civil war; Ecuador's 2025 fuel-subsidy cancellation triggered Indigenous-led national strikes and a state of emergency in several provinces.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: The compensating-transfer promise is consistently outrun by the speed and visibility of the price shock — unrest arrives before, or instead of, promised mitigation reaching this actor.

stated_vs_revealed.stated: Kenya's 2024 Finance Bill was presented by the government as a necessary, technocratic revenue-and-IMF-compliance measure, without emphasis on its direct impact on subsistence-level households.
stated_vs_revealed.revealed: Youth-led #RejectFinanceBill2024 protests (18 Jun-8 Aug 2024) escalated to demonstrators storming and partially burning Parliament on 25 June, causing 80+ deaths and 230+ injuries; President Ruto declined to sign the bill on 26 June and it was formally withdrawn on 28 June — a full policy reversal within roughly 10 days of the peak protest.
stated_vs_revealed.delta: A measure framed as technocratic was understood immediately by the affected population as a direct threat to subsistence, producing the fastest state capitulation among the cases sampled.

tripwires.if: a fuel or staple-food subsidy is removed or a price cap lifted without a pre-funded, already-distributed compensating transfer
tripwires.then: protest/riot probability spikes within roughly 2-8 weeks (Nigeria 2023, Angola 2025, Ecuador 2025, Kenya 2024 pattern), materially faster than typical policy-review or IMF-review timelines

tripwires.if: protest coordination is captured by an organised network (union, opposition party, diaspora-linked social-media campaign)
tripwires.then: the 'hard' constraint against organised uprising effectively breaks and unrest scales past issue-specific protest toward broader regime-legitimacy contestation (Kenya 2024 precedent)

what_would_change_my_mind: A major, poorly-compensated subsidy removal in a fragile state (2026-27) that produces no protest/riot response within the historical 2-8 week window would suggest the mechanism is weakening (fatigue, repression capacity, or effective pre-distribution). Migration-flow magnitudes specifically are low-confidence: intention surveys are a poor proxy and this pass did not obtain hard cross-border flow data matched to a specific subsidy-shock episode.
